basis.governing_question: Should Quinta Azul enter the Spanish retail market and, if so, how?

phases.name: Research
phases.objective_one_line: Assess the size, competition and buyer needs of the Spanish retail market and Quinta Azul's capability to win there.

gate.label: Findings sign-off
gate.decision: Is Spain attractive enough to justify designing entry options?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Compare entry options for Spain, build the business case and draft the entry roadmap for the go or no-go.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the Spain go or no-go decision and, if go, the entry plan?

workstreams.name: Spain market attractiveness
workstreams.answers: How large and attractive is the Spanish retail market for Quinta Azul's olive oil?
activities: Size Spanish retail olive-oil demand and growth by segment
Review published market reports and retail sales data
Assess regulation and retail channel structure in Spain

workstreams.name: Competition and buyer needs
workstreams.answers: Who competes in Spanish retail, and what do retail buyers and shoppers there need?
activities: Profile competitors selling olive oil in Spanish retail
Interview Spanish retail buyers and shoppers on their needs
Compare competitor pricing, ranges and shelf presence

workstreams.name: Capability to win in Spain
workstreams.answers: Does Quinta Azul have the assets and capabilities to win in Spanish retail?
activities: Interview the CEO, Commercial Director and operations staff
Review Quinta Azul's production and sales data
Assess gaps between Quinta Azul's assets and buyer needs

workstreams.name: Entry options for Spain
workstreams.answers: Which entry options exist for Spain, and how do they compare on agreed criteria?
activities: Define the entry options for Spanish retail
Test the options with retail buyers and Quinta Azul's staff
Compare the options on criteria agreed with Quinta Azul

workstreams.name: Spain business case
workstreams.answers: Does the business case for the preferred entry option support a go or no-go on Spain?
activities: Model revenue, cost and investment for the preferred option
Draw cost inputs from Quinta Azul's operational data
Set out the risks and assumptions behind the go or no-go

workstreams.name: Spain entry roadmap
workstreams.answers: If the answer is go, what entry plan and roadmap should Quinta Azul follow in Spain?
activities: Draft the entry roadmap if the answer is go
Define owners and decisions needed for each entry step
Check the draft roadmap with the people who would run it

deliverables.name: Spanish retail olive-oil market size and growth by segment
Competitor profiles and buyer needs in Spanish retail
Gap assessment of Quinta Azul's assets for Spanish retail
Findings pack on Spain's attractiveness for sign-off
Spain entry options compared on agreed criteria
Business case for the preferred Spain entry option
Spain entry roadmap with owners and decisions per step
Spain go or no-go decision pack with entry plan

events.label: Kick-off
events.purpose: Align on scope and secure data access
events.decision: Can Quinta Azul open access to sales data and Spanish retail contacts?
agenda: Present the assessment objective and the Research plan
Review the data and people access the evidence work needs
Decide on access to sales data and retail contacts

events.label: Check-in: market size
events.purpose: Review market size and growth findings
events.decision: Which Spanish retail segments should the findings pack focus on?
agenda: Present market size and growth by segment
Discuss what the segments mean for the remaining Research work
Decide the segments the findings pack should focus on

events.label: Findings sign-off
events.decision: Is Spain attractive enough to justify designing entry options?
agenda: Present the findings pack on Spain's attractiveness
Review competitor profiles, buyer needs and the gap assessment
Decide whether Spain justifies designing entry options

events.label: Check-in: entry options
events.purpose: Review entry options before the roadmap
events.decision: Which Spain entry option should the roadmap and decision pack detail?
agenda: Present the entry options compared on agreed criteria
Discuss the trade-offs between the options
Decide which option the roadmap and decision pack detail

events.label: Final readout
events.purpose: Approve the Spain go or no-go decision
events.decision: Approve the Spain go or no-go decision and, if go, the entry plan?
agenda: Present the business case and the entry roadmap
Review the go or no-go decision pack and entry plan
Decide on approval of the go or no-go and the entry plan

architect_notes: Engagement length is not given, so the 7 to 10 weeks are an estimate from the sizing; confirm length and any deadline before quoting.
Design is sized for a go outcome; a no-go would drop the entry roadmap and shorten the phase.

sub_questions.question: How large and attractive is the Spanish retail market for Quinta Azul's olive oil?
Who competes there, and what do Spanish retail buyers and shoppers need?
Does Quinta Azul have the assets and capabilities to win in Spain?
Which entry options exist for Spain, and does the business case support a go or no-go?
If the answer is go, what entry plan and roadmap should Quinta Azul follow?

phases.name: Research

work.unit: Market assessed in full (demand, channels, competitors, regulation, buyer interviews)

phases.why: Spain is assessed as one market in full; the capability check and leadership interviews run alongside it.

phases.name: Design

work.unit: Entry option and business case for one market
Entry sequence and roadmap across markets

phases.why: The entry option and business case for Spain come first, then the entry roadmap, one after the other.

sizing.levers: Assessing only the retail channels the CEO and Commercial Director prioritize, and starting the roadmap alongside the business case, would shorten the engagement most.
